facts.fact: The Gambia Information Commission's chairperson speaks of implementing the Access to Information Act, with six institutions having appointed information officers.
The Gambia Information Commission is in operation under its chairperson, who says draft regulations, validated, are with the Ministry of Justice.
The Information Commission's chairperson, Neneh MacDouall-Gaye, said in October 2025 that the Commission had received 15 complaints since its establishment.
The Republic says the Access to Information Act empowers the public to request information from public institutions, with sections 9 and 17 operating.
The Republic reports it filed appeals against six institutions before Gambia's Access to Information Commission, which the Act provides for.
The Standard reports the National Assembly passed the ATI Bill in July 2021 and President Barrow assented to it.

The Standard reports the Access to Information Commission, through its chairperson, said it is reviewing complaints against six institutions and has written to all public institutions about implementation plans.
